senses.gloss: भ्रमर- + करण्डक भ्रमर- + करण्डक, m. (?) a dark lantern, Daśak. in Chr. 186, 11.
भ्रमत्कुटी भ्रमत्कुटी, i. e. भ्रमन्त्-, f. a sort of umbrella.
भ्रातृ-पद्म-वन भ्रातृ-पद्म-वन, n. a group of lotus-like brothers.

भ्रंश् भ्रंश्, and (erroneously) भ्रंस् भ्रंस्, i. 4, भ्रश्य (cf. भ्रश्), भ्रस्य, Par. (also Ātm., e. g. Pañc. iv. d. 39), and † i. 1, Par. Ātm.
 1. To fall, Sund. 1, 15; to fall down, Pañc. i. d. 146.
 2. To be lost, Rām. 3, 54, 20.
 3. To run away, to flee from [] (abl.), Bhaṭṭ. 14, 105.
 4. To be deprived (with abl.), Man. 7, 111; Pañc. iv. d. 39 (with स् and Ātm.).
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass. भ्रष्ट.
 1. Fallen, Hit. i. d. 168 (स्थान-, adj. Having lost their rank).
 2. Lost.
 3. Deprived of, Bhag. 6, 11.
 4. Deviated, Pañc. 228, 14.
 5. Fallen from virtue, wicked.
 --Comp.
 --Caus. भ्रंशय.
 1. To expel, MBh. 3, 8759.
 2. To deprive, MBh. 3, 1571. भ्रंशित, Deprived, Chr. 48, 2.
 --With the prep. अप अप, अपभ्रष्ट, Corrupted (as speech), Kathās. 17, 41.
 --With परि परि, To be deprived (with abl.), Hit. i. d. 128. परिभ्रष्ट,
 1. Fallen, Pañc. 188, 15.
 2. Degraded.
 3. Deprived of (instr.), Pañc. iii. d. 55; Man. 10, 20.
 4. Lost, Nal. 18, 10.
 --With प्र प्र,
 1. To fall, Ragh. 14, 54 (Calc.).
 2. To be deprived, Mṛcch. 14, 12 (Calc.). प्रभ्रेष्ट,
 1. Fallen, dropping, fallen off.
 2. Broken.
 --Caus. To throw down from (abl.), Ragh. 13, 36 (Calc.). प्रभ्रंशित, Expelled, MBh. 3, 601.
 --With वि वि, विभ्रष्ट,
 1. Broken off, or from.
 2. Fallen.
 3. Separated.
 4. Deprived, MBh. 3, 3.
 5. Lost.
 --Caus. To deprive, Chr. 21, 6.
 --Cf. A.S. hreósan and reosan, To fall; Goth. ur-risan; A.S. arisan, To rise; Goth. us-hrisjan and af-hrisjan (Caus.), To cast off.
भ्रंस् भ्रंस्, भ्रंसिन् भ्रंसिन्, see भ्रंश्, भ्रंशिन्.

भ्रंश भ्रंश् + अ, m.
 1. Falling.
 2. Declining from a height, or from propriety, ruin, Bhag. 2, 63.
 3. Falling off, Megh. 2.
 4. Abandoning, dropping, Pañc. iii. d. 246; desertion, Pañc. 145, 10.
 5. Losing, Pañc. 68, 22; loss, Rājat. 5, 307; Hit. iii. d. 5 (स्थान-भ्रंशं ययुः, They did lose their nest).
 --Comp.

भ्रंशिन् भ्रंश् + इन्, भ्रंसिन् भ्रंस् + इन्, adj., f. नी.
 1. Falling, Megh. 30; Śāk. 1, 7.
 2. Causing to fall (स्व-अर्थ-, injuring, or detrimental to, our interest), Pañc. 248, 18.
 --Comp.
भ्रकुंश and ˚स भ्रकुंश, ˚स, see भृकुंश.
भ्रकुटि भ्रकुटि, see भ्रूकुटि.
† भ्रक्ष् भ्रक्ष्, v. r. of भक्ष्.

भ्रज्ज् भ्रज्ज्, i. 6, भृज्ज, Par. Ātm. To boil or fry, Bhaṭṭ. 14, 86; the base of many forms in भर्ज्.
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass. भृष्ट.
 --Comp.
 --Cf. Lat. frigere, frictus, frixus (= भृक्त, see भृज्); ϕρύγω; O.H.G. briuwan; A.S. briwan; and O.N. brugga, To brew.

भ्राज् भ्राज् (probably अभि-राज्), i. 1, Ātm. (in ved. and epic poetry also Par., MBh. 4, 219).
 1. To shine, to beam, Chr. 289, 3 = Rigv. i. 50, 3 (Par.).
 --Caus. To illuminate, MBh. 3, 15579.
 --With the prep. वि वि, To shine brilliantly, Chr. 291, 4 = Rigv. i. 85, 4; Rām. 3, 52, 25.
 --Cf. भृज्; Lat. flagrare, flamma (for flagma), flamen, fulgur, fulgere, fulmen, fulvus, etc.; Goth. bairhts; A.S. bearht, beorht; O.H.G. beraht, blanch, blich, blichan; ϕλέγω, ϕλόξ; probably also A.S. blác, blaecan, blícan.
† भ्रण् भ्रण्, i. 1, Par. To sound (cf. भ्रम् and रण्).
भ्रभङ्ग भ्रभङ्ग, m. A frown (cf. भ्रू-भङ्ग, s. v. भङ्ग, and भ्रकुंश, भ्रकुटि).

भ्रम् भ्रम्, i. 1 and 4, भ्राम्य, Par. (in epic poetry also Ātm., MBh. 3, 12228), originally, The flying about and humming of insects.
 1. To turn round, to move circularly, to whirl, Pañc. v. d. 20.
 2. † To be unsteady or unfixed.
 3. To stray, to roam, to wander, Pañc. 43, 4; i. d. 446; to go astray, Pañc. v. d. 68 (Ātm.).
 4. To wander over (acc.), MBh. 1, 5184.
 5. To surround, Rājat. 5, 146.
 6. To mistake.
 7. † To be ignorant.
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass. भ्रान्त.
 1. Being wandered over (with acc.). Bhartṛ. 3, 4. []
 2. Running, Arj. 4, 38; rolling, Chr. 35, 2.
 3. Whirled.
 4. Confused, Rām. 3, 55, 36.
 5. Blundering. n. Roaming, Bhartṛ. 2, 11.
 --Caus. भ्रमय (in epic poetry also भ्रामय, also Pañc. 263, 8. or i. 4, Ātm.).
 1. To turn round, Bhag. 18, 61; to whirl, MBh. 2, 762.
 2. To move to and fro (without getting a way of egress), Rām. 1, 44, 12.
 3. To agitate, Utt. Rāmac. 23, 8.
 --With the prep. उद् उद्,
 1. To jump out of (abl.), Draup. 8, 19.
 2. To be beside one's self, Daśak. in Chr. 183, 17 (read उद्भ्रम्य). उद्-भ्रान्त,
 1. Flying upward, Rām. 6, 83, 26.
 2. Whirled on, thrown up, Hit. iii. d. 140.
 3. Whirling on, Utt. Rāmac. 138, 4.
 4. Bewildered, Pañc. 141, 4.
 --With परि परि,
 1. To walk round about, Pañc. 230, 16.
 2. To roam about, Hit. 76, 6, M.M.; Pañc. 21, 1.
 3. To fly round about, Pañc. 148, 10.
 --With वि वि, To rove, Nalod. 3, 26.
 2. To wander over, MBh. 3, 2648.
 3. † To play, to wanton. वि-भ्रान्त,
 1. Agitated, Bhag. 16, 16.
 2. Hurried.
 --Comp.
 --With मस् सम्, संभ्रान्त, Agitated, confused, Utt. Rāmac. 50, 3; troubled, Śāk. 12, 17.
 --Comp.
 --Cf. भ्रमर; Lat. fremere; O.H.G. breman; A.S. bremman; O.H.G. bremo, briosa; N.G. brausen; πεμϕρηδών, ϕριμάσσομαι, βρέμω, βροντή, βαϐράζω, βαϐραδών, etc.

भ्रम भ्रम् + अ, m.
 1. Whirling, going round, Rājat. 5, 363.
 2. Straying, roaming.
 3. Error, Bhāṣāp. 133.
 4. A whirlpool.
 5. A watercourse.
 6. A potter's wheel.

भ्रमण भ्रमण, i. e. भ्रम् + अन, []
 I. n.
 1. Whirling, turning round, Bhāṣāp. 6.
 2. Giddiness, Lass. 17, 5.
 3. Wandering, Vikr. 23, 11.
 II. f. णी,
 A sort of game performed by women for the amusement of a lover or husband.

भ्रमर भ्रम् + अर,
 I. m.
 1. A (large black) bee, Vikr. 64, 1.
 2. A lover, a gallant.
 II. n. Epilepsy.

भ्रामर भ्रामर, i. e. भ्रमर + अ,
 I. m. A sort of loadstone.
 II. f. री,
 1. Pārvatī,
 2. A female attendant on Durgā.
 III. n.
 1. Honey.
 2. Whirling round.
 3. Epilepsy.
 4. A kind of dancing.
 5. A village.

भ्रमि भ्रम् + इ, f.
 1. Going round, turning about, Utt. Rāmac. 66, 4.
 2. A lathe, Kāśīkh. 17, 117.
भ्रश् भ्रश्, i. 4, Par. To fall, impersonal pass., Śiś. 9, 73 (it was fallen by the mirror = the mirror fell); cf. भ्रंश्.
भ्राश् भ्राश्, and † म्रास् भ्रास्, † भ्राश् भ्लाश्, and † भ्रास् भ्लास्, i. 1. and 4, Ātm. To shine; cf. भ्राज्.
भ्रास् भ्रास्, see भ्रश्.
भ्रष्टाधिकारत्व भ्रष्टाधिकारत्व, i. e. भ्रष्ट-अधिकार्च् + त्व (vb. भ्रंश्), n. Loss of office, Pañc. 22, 11.
भ्राजदृष्टि भ्राजदृष्टि, i. e. भ्राजन्त्-ऋष्टि, adj. Having shining swords (i. e. lightnings), Chr. 290, 11 = Rigv. i. 64, 11.
भ्राजिष्णु भ्राज् + इष्णु, adj. Splendid, elegant.

भ्रातृ भ्रातृ, i. e. भृ + आ + तृ, m.
 1. A brother, Chr. 3, 5; du. तरौ, Brother and sister.
 2. A friend, Megh. 10. []
 --Comp.
 --Cf. Lat. frater; ϕράτηρ and ϕρατήρ, ϕατρία, etc.; Goth. brothar; A.S. bródhor.

भ्रातृव्य भ्रातृ + व्य, m.
 1.
 A brother's son.
 2. An enemy.
 --Cf. Lat. fratrūelis.

भ्रात्रीय भ्रात्रीय, i. e. भ्रातृ + ईय,
 I. adj. Fraternal.
 II. m. A brother's son.

भ्रान्ति भ्रान्ति, i. e. भ्रम् + ति, f.
 1. Going round, whirling, rolling, Vikr. d. 4.
 2. Wandering.
 3. Error, Bṛhaspati ap. Cowell, Kusumāñjali, transl. p. 65, n. †; Pañc. 50, 10 (कुमुद-भ्रान्तिं जनयति मत्स्यानाम्, Causes the fishes to mistake him for a lotusflower). चन्दन-, instr. Mistaking (it) for a sandal tree, Utt. Rāmac. 29, 8.

भ्रामक भ्रामक, i. e. भ्रम्, Caus. + अक,
 I. adj. Causing to whirl.
 II. m.
 1. A cheat.
 2. A jackal.
 3. The sun-flower.
 4. A sort of loadstone.

भ्रामरिन् भ्रामरिन्, i. e. भ्रामर + इन्, adj., f. इणी.
 1. Made of honey.
 2. Whirling.
 3. Epileptic, Man. 3, 161.

भ्राष्ट्र भ्राष्ट्र, i. e. भ्राज् + त्र (cf. भृज्),
 I. m. (and n.), A frying-pan, Pañc. i. d. 148.
 II. n. Æther.
भ्रातृ- + संघातवन्त् भ्रातृ- + संघातवन्त्, i. e. भ्रातृसंघात + चन्त्, m. having many brothers, Pañc. iii. d. 8.
